raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Concurrent requests for the same external prefix currently allocate separate GPU destinations, or wait behind connector-side load gating. This change lets eligible followers attach to the initiating request's blocks with ordinary block-pool reference counts and wait for one transfer.

The scheduler tracks exact pending prefixes using existing prefix-cache hashes. It publishes successful loads before releasing an aborted initiating request and wakes every remaining follower. Cancelling a follower releases only its references. Failed loads either fail affected requests or detach all readers before recomputation; pending entries also prevent connector-cache resets.

Initial support is opt-in, enabled for the built-in CPUOffloadingSpec with built-in LRU/ARC policies: prefix caching enabled, one FullAttentionSpec group, exact contiguous block-aligned partial-prompt hits, including hits extending a local prefix. Full-prompt hits, speculative decoding, context parallelism, encoder inputs, custom specs/policies, and other connectors retain existing behavior. Cache salts and token-hash isolation remain intact.

Addresses #44882. Duplicate checks covered the issue comments, open PRs referencing the issue, and related area searches. #48189 was closed without merging. Open #44295 changes connector-side convoy handling; it does not implement shared core allocation or this lifecycle. #53067 and #55724 address connector context and async admission respectively.

Validation:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  -q --maxfail=3 --confcutdir=tests/v1
```

634 passed after merging main (`f26d9f432c`) on October 11; the latest merge resolves a test import conflict without changing the sharing implementation. The refresh uses the existing KV-holding waiting queue for shared followers and tracks their KV-fetch stages; cancellation cases verify those counts return to zero. Includes the request-level receive-failure regression tests. Regression tests cover one allocation/load, reference ownership, initiating-request/follower cancellation, late followers, local-prefix extension, isolation, both failure policies, early/final block-level transfer errors, request-level failed_recving (including aborted owners), and cleanup. The four new request-level failure cases reproduced the bug before the fix and pass afterward. Real CPU-offload scheduler integration emits one load job and shares block IDs in both synchronous and asynchronous scheduling modes; worker completion is simulated.

`SSL_CERT_FILE=<environment certifi bundle> .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <six changed files>` passed all applicable hooks, including the current mypy hook (Python 3.11 target), ruff, test tethering, and SPDX checks. `git diff origin/main --check` also passed. The first hook setup attempt failed on a local Node-download certificate error; retrying with the existing certificate bundle succeeded.

Local GPU execution, model-output/accuracy evaluation, and hardware latency/throughput benchmarks were unavailable on macOS arm64 (no CUDA or XPU).

External GPU evidence: [LysanderPhong reported five successful executions](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418#issuecomment-6094266885) on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop using PR commit `244daac75b` and native baseline `231fdb83cc`: sync/async sharing and capability opt-out, real CPU↔GPU copies, exact synthetic FP16 bytes, private tails, and cleanup. The attached archive/test SHA256 checksums and original logs/JSON were reviewed and agree with those claims; execution was not independently repeated. This evidence does not validate the October 10 refresh, pending-transfer cancellation/failure, model outputs, performance, or multi-rank behavior. The evidence-oriented candidate test is not included in this diff; the current main worker layout APIs have also changed. GPU lifecycle and model-output validation remain outstanding before merge; no hardware performance claim is made.

AI assistance: implementation, tests, and this description were prepared with OpenAI Codex. The human submitter previously confirmed reviewing every changed line and personally running the relevant tests for the earlier revision. The October 10 queue/statistics refresh and October 11 merge still require human review and testing. GPU/model evaluation remains outstanding as described above.

CC @GentleCold @orozery @natoscott — feedback on shared external-prefix loading and cancellation semantics would be appreciated.

`failed_recving` also needs to mark the shared load as failed. The connector contract guarantees that failed receives are included in `finished_recving`, but `_complete_shared_prefix_load()` only observes failures reported through `invalid_block_ids`.

If the owner reports `finished_recving={owner_id}` and `failed_recving={owner_id}` without invalid block IDs, the entry is still published through `cache_blocks()` and all followers are released. Under `failure_policy="fail"`, only the owner is failed; under `"recompute"`, only the owner is reset, so followers can run on the failed shared destination.

Please propagate request-level receive failure to the shared entry and all participants before publishing or waking them, and add tests for `failed_recving` under both failure policies, including the case where the owner has already been aborted. The tests should verify that followers either receive `FINISHED_ERROR` or release the shared blocks and recompute locally, and that failed blocks never enter the normal prefix cache.

The four added regression cases reproduced the bug before the fix and now pass under both failure policies. They check that failed destinations are never published to the prefix cache and that followers either fail or release their references and recompute locally.

Could you take another look at the failure propagation and lifecycle handling when you have time?

Hi @zayedu. I'm coming at the same problem from the RL side. In GRPO-style rollout we sample n responses per prompt, so a group of requests shares one long prefix and hits the decode instance at roughly the same time. Under PD with NIXL that prefix gets pulled n times: when the siblings are scheduled, the first load hasn't published to the prefix cache yet, so none of them hit.

Your PR looks like it already covers the core of that — the shared block and refcount, the supports_shared_prefix_loads() contract, and the owner/follower abort and failure paths. What I don't think is covered yet is NIXL, which brings its own questions: what makes two requests safe to share (model/KV namespace, TP layout, the per-request transfer lease on the P side), keeping the pull alive when the owner aborts while followers are still waiting, and making sure each P-side request still gets released.

I want to help this, so I want to ask two questions:
1. Is extending this to NIXL already on your roadmap? If so I'd rather help
   than duplicate.
2. If not, would you be open to me picking that piece up on top of your
   contract? I'd work against your branch and follow whatever shape you've
   settled on.

Either way I can bring data. I have multi-GPU/multi-node hardware and a real RL rollout workload, so I can measure what a cold GRPO group actually costs today on 1P+1D NIXL — duplicate transfers, bytes on the wire, unique GPU blocks — and post it here as a baseline. I can run it if you like.

Thanks—I'll proceed with a separate NIXL follow-up against this branch and track contract changes during review.

I'll first share a cold 1P+1D GRPO baseline with transfer counts/overlap, transferred payload bytes, unique destination GPU blocks, and TTFT, together with the model, prefix length, concurrency, TP configuration, and exact revisions. Each sibling will have its own producer request/lease. The implementation will cover compatibility checks, keeping the owner's transfer and lease alive through cancellation while readers remain, and releasing every producer-side request.

One integration detail surfaced in the code: the current core sharing path requires a partial, block-aligned prefix, whereas ordinary NIXL loads can cover the full prompt. I'm investigating sharing only the immutable full-block prefix of that load, with private tails for followers, while preserving the existing CPU-offload defaults. I'll include concrete lifecycle and output-correctness tests.

Here is the **cold 1P+1D GRPO-shaped baseline** on main Python source `0af3441`.

Qwen3-0.6B BF16 ran on two GB200 GPUs on the same node, with TP1 per server, NIXL pull, 128-token blocks and prefix caching. Each group used a fresh D cache salt. All P requests finished before concurrent D submission.

We measured 10 groups per configuration without tracing, after 2 excluded warmup groups. All 260 measured D requests succeeded.

| Prompt tokens | Concurrent requests | Transfers/group | Payload MiB/group | D TTFT (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 1 | 1 | 448 | 69.49 |
| 4096 | 4 | 4 | 1792 | 105.83 |
| 4096 | 8 | 8 | 546 | 142.00 |
| 4097 | 1 | 1 | 462 | 60.20 |
| 4097 | 4 | 4 | 1848 | 77.60 |
| 4097 | 8 | 8 | 560 (6 groups), 1008 (4 groups) | 141.59 |

Payload counts connector bytes. TTFT is the median of the 10 group medians, measured from D submission to first output text.

**At concurrency 8, existing D prefix caching already reduces transferred bytes.** Cold means no cached prefix at the start of each group. It still allows reuse within that group.

A separate single-group trace counted the unique GPU blocks written by READs on D at concurrency 4: **128** for 4096 tokens and **132** for 4097 tokens. In both cases, the shared physical prefix was read four times.

[Full results and reproduction](https://github.com/NolenLiang/vllm/tree/rl/nixl-shared-prefix-evidence-20260929/nixl-shared-prefix-evidence) include timing ranges and runtime versions. The NIXL follow-up is in #59141. Repeated untraced candidate comparisons remain pending.

Hi @zayedu — I’m sharing a test-only candidate for the outstanding real GPU transfer validation on this PR.

The test runs against PR head `244daac75b3311df5c5367cd671d21070ca1f309`, with the matching native baseline `231fdb83cccf18b0c96ab874fe210820025b3857`. It adds one test file and leaves your production implementation unchanged.

It combines the native scheduler / `CPUOffloadingSpec` shared-prefix admission with real CPU↔GPU copies. Two 48-token requests share a 32-token prefix and have different 16-token tails. Synthetic FP16 data is first stored through the native worker, GPU storage is poisoned, and both requests are admitted before worker dispatch.

**Results on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop / SM120, WSL2, driver 592.01, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1:**

- Sync and async scheduler variants each passed in two fresh processes; one capability opt-out control also passed: **five successful executions of three distinct variants**.
- Each positive execution shared the same two nonempty GPU prefix blocks with refcount two and one logical load job. Native seed-store and load completions each reported **65,536 bytes**.
- Both real request block tables matched independent expected bytes exactly. The test checks guards, CPU source contents, private-tail separation, reference/job cleanup, and successful closure of the saved native mmap handle.
- The opt-out control did not attach in flight; subsequent ordinary cache reuse was allowed. Logical jobs are not physical DMA/kernel counts.

The attachment contains an applicable `TEST_ADDITION.patch`, exact test source, reproduction notes, commands, and the five per-case JSON records and original pytest logs. Two earlier fixture revisions failed before this final version (a pathname-lifetime assumption, then incomplete mmap closure); those runs are not counted as full passes. The successful fixture correction does not establish an upstream leak or the old process’s unique root cause.

**Scope:** model computation is substituted by model-output containers. This does not validate model outputs/accuracy, performance, cancellation/failure, multi-rank, NIXL, current main, or production readiness. Host memory was unpinned on WSL; full-process GPU-memory telemetry was unavailable. Full upstream CI/pre-commit was not run.

**AI disclosure:** Codex prepared the test and executed it on my local GPU. A separate GPT Pro review checked the code and raw evidence offline without repeating GPU execution. This is not an attestation of manual human code review or upstream CI.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("abort_owner", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+def test_core_shares_cpu_offload_load_and_blocks(abort_owner, async_scheduling):
+    """The built-in CPU cache emits one load even when its owner is aborted."""
+    config = create_vllm_config(
+        kv_connector="OffloadingConnector",
+        kv_role="kv_both",
+        kv_connector_extra_config={"cpu_bytes_to_use": 1048576},
+    )
+    config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = async_scheduling
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        config, num_blocks=16, kv_cache_config=_make_kv_cache_config()
+    )
+    connector = scheduler.connector.connector_scheduler
+    owner, follower = [
+        create_request(num_tokens=48, common_prefix_len=32) for _ in range(2)
+    ]
+    for request in (owner, follower):
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+    context = connector._req_status[owner.request_id].req_context
+    keys = [make_offload_key(h, 0) for h in owner.block_hashes[:2]]
+    connector.manager.prepare_store(keys, context)
+    connector.manager.complete_store(keys, context)
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    jobs = output.kv_connector_metadata.load_jobs
+    assert len(jobs) == 1
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+    assert manager.get_block_ids(owner.request_id) == manager.get_block_ids(
+        follower.request_id
+    )
+    blocks = list(manager.get_blocks(owner.request_id).blocks[0])
+    assert all(block.ref_cnt == 2 for block in blocks)
+    if abort_owner:
+        scheduler.finish_requests(owner.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+
+    result = create_model_runner_output(reqs=[], finished_recving={owner.request_id})
+    result.kv_connector_output.kv_connector_worker_meta = OffloadingWorkerMetadata(
+        completed_jobs={job_id: 1 for job_id in jobs}
+    )
+    scheduler.update_from_output(output, result)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert not output.kv_connector_metadata.load_jobs
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens[follower.request_id] == 16
+    assert manager.get_blocks(follower.request_id).blocks[0][:2] == blocks
+    assert all(job.is_store for job in connector._jobs.values())
+    assert not connector._chunks_being_loaded
+    result = create_model_runner_output(
+        reqs=[r for r in (owner, follower) if not r.is_finished()], use_eos=True
+    )
+    result.kv_connector_output = KVConnectorOutput(
+        kv_connector_worker_meta=OffloadingWorkerMetadata(
+            completed_jobs={job_id: 1 for job_id in connector._jobs}
+        )
+    )
+    scheduler.update_from_output(output, result)
+    scheduler.schedule()
+    assert not connector._req_status
+    assert not connector._jobs
+    assert all(block.ref_cnt == 0 for block in blocks)
+

+def _shared_load_scheduler(monkeypatch, policy="recompute", matched_tokens=32):
+    config = create_vllm_config(
+        kv_connector="MockKVConnector",
+        kv_connector_extra_config={
+            "matched_tokens": matched_tokens,
+            "is_async": True,
+        },
+        kv_load_failure_policy=policy,
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(config, num_blocks=32)
+    connector = scheduler.connector
+    monkeypatch.setattr(connector, "supports_shared_prefix_loads", lambda: True)
+    connector.update_state_after_alloc = Mock()
+    return scheduler
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cancel", [None, "owner", "follower", "both"])
+def test_shared_external_prefix_lifetime(monkeypatch, cancel):
+    """One transfer owns the write; aborting either reader preserves the other."""
+    scheduler = _shared_load_scheduler(monkeypatch)
+    owner, follower = [
+        create_request(num_tokens=48, common_prefix_len=32) for _ in range(2)
+    ]
+    for request in (owner, follower):
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+    blocks = list(manager.get_blocks(owner.request_id).blocks[0])
+    assert manager.get_block_ids(owner.request_id) == manager.get_block_ids(
+        follower.request_id
+    )
+    assert len(blocks) == 2
+    assert all(block.ref_cnt == 2 and block.block_hash is None for block in blocks)
+    assert scheduler.connector.update_state_after_alloc.call_count == 1
+    assert not output.num_scheduled_tokens
+    assert not scheduler.reset_connector_cache()
+    assert _kv_fetch_stages(scheduler) == (0, 2, 0)
+
+    if cancel in ("owner", "both"):
+        scheduler.finish_requests(owner.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    if cancel in ("follower", "both"):
+        scheduler.finish_requests(follower.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    # The owner pins the destination until the transfer reports completion.
+    assert all(block.ref_cnt >= 1 for block in blocks)
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        output,
+        create_model_runner_output(reqs=[], finished_recving={owner.request_id}),
+    )
+    active = [r for r in (owner, follower) if not r.is_finished()]
+    assert _kv_fetch_stages(scheduler) == (0, 0, len(active))
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert set(output.num_scheduled_tokens) == {r.request_id for r in active}
+    assert _kv_fetch_stages(scheduler) == (0, 0, 0)
+    for request in active:
+        assert manager.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks[0][:2] == blocks
+        assert output.num_scheduled_tokens[request.request_id] == 16
+    assert all(block.ref_cnt == len(active) for block in blocks)
+    assert not scheduler._shared_prefix_loads
+    assert not scheduler._shared_load_followers
+    scheduler.finish_requests(None, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    scheduler.schedule()
+    assert_scheduler_empty(scheduler)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("policy", ["recompute", "fail"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("abort_owner", [False, True])

+    "error_kind,early_error",

+    scheduler = _shared_load_scheduler(monkeypatch, policy)
+    owner, follower = [

+    ]

`failed_recving` also needs to mark the shared load as failed. The connector contract guarantees that failed receives are included in `finished_recving`, but `_complete_shared_prefix_load()` only observes failures reported through `invalid_block_ids`.

If the owner reports `finished_recving={owner_id}` and `failed_recving={owner_id}` without invalid block IDs, the entry is still published through `cache_blocks()` and all followers are released. Under `failure_policy="fail"`, only the owner is failed; under `"recompute"`, only the owner is reset, so followers can run on the failed shared destination.

Please propagate request-level receive failure to the shared entry and all participants before publishing or waking them, and add tests for `failed_recving` under both failure policies, including the case where the owner has already been aborted. The tests should verify that followers either receive `FINISHED_ERROR` or release the shared blocks and recompute locally, and that failed blocks never enter the normal prefix cache.

Hi @zayedu. I'm coming at the same problem from the RL side. In GRPO-style rollout we sample n responses per prompt, so a group of requests shares one long prefix and hits the decode instance at roughly the same time. Under PD with NIXL that prefix gets pulled n times: when the siblings are scheduled, the first load hasn't published to the prefix cache yet, so none of them hit.

Your PR looks like it already covers the core of that — the shared block and refcount, the supports_shared_prefix_loads() contract, and the owner/follower abort and failure paths. What I don't think is covered yet is NIXL, which brings its own questions: what makes two requests safe to share (model/KV namespace, TP layout, the per-request transfer lease on the P side), keeping the pull alive when the owner aborts while followers are still waiting, and making sure each P-side request still gets released.

I want to help this, so I want to ask two questions:
1. Is extending this to NIXL already on your roadmap? If so I'd rather help
   than duplicate.
2. If not, would you be open to me picking that piece up on top of your
   contract? I'd work against your branch and follow whatever shape you've
   settled on.

Either way I can bring data. I have multi-GPU/multi-node hardware and a real RL rollout workload, so I can measure what a cold GRPO group actually costs today on 1P+1D NIXL — duplicate transfers, bytes on the wire, unique GPU blocks — and post it here as a baseline. I can run it if you like.

Thanks—I'll proceed with a separate NIXL follow-up against this branch and track contract changes during review.

I'll first share a cold 1P+1D GRPO baseline with transfer counts/overlap, transferred payload bytes, unique destination GPU blocks, and TTFT, together with the model, prefix length, concurrency, TP configuration, and exact revisions. Each sibling will have its own producer request/lease. The implementation will cover compatibility checks, keeping the owner's transfer and lease alive through cancellation while readers remain, and releasing every producer-side request.

One integration detail surfaced in the code: the current core sharing path requires a partial, block-aligned prefix, whereas ordinary NIXL loads can cover the full prompt. I'm investigating sharing only the immutable full-block prefix of that load, with private tails for followers, while preserving the existing CPU-offload defaults. I'll include concrete lifecycle and output-correctness tests.

Here is the **cold 1P+1D GRPO-shaped baseline** on main Python source `0af3441`.

Qwen3-0.6B BF16 ran on two GB200 GPUs on the same node, with TP1 per server, NIXL pull, 128-token blocks and prefix caching. Each group used a fresh D cache salt. All P requests finished before concurrent D submission.

We measured 10 groups per configuration without tracing, after 2 excluded warmup groups. All 260 measured D requests succeeded.

| Prompt tokens | Concurrent requests | Transfers/group | Payload MiB/group | D TTFT (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | 1 | 1 | 448 | 69.49 |
| 4096 | 4 | 4 | 1792 | 105.83 |
| 4096 | 8 | 8 | 546 | 142.00 |
| 4097 | 1 | 1 | 462 | 60.20 |
| 4097 | 4 | 4 | 1848 | 77.60 |
| 4097 | 8 | 8 | 560 (6 groups), 1008 (4 groups) | 141.59 |

Payload counts connector bytes. TTFT is the median of the 10 group medians, measured from D submission to first output text.

**At concurrency 8, existing D prefix caching already reduces transferred bytes.** Cold means no cached prefix at the start of each group. It still allows reuse within that group.

A separate single-group trace counted the unique GPU blocks written by READs on D at concurrency 4: **128** for 4096 tokens and **132** for 4097 tokens. In both cases, the shared physical prefix was read four times.

[Full results and reproduction](https://github.com/NolenLiang/vllm/tree/rl/nixl-shared-prefix-evidence-20260929/nixl-shared-prefix-evidence) include timing ranges and runtime versions. The NIXL follow-up is in #59141. Repeated untraced candidate comparisons remain pending.

The test runs against PR head `244daac75b3311df5c5367cd671d21070ca1f309`, with the matching native baseline `231fdb83cccf18b0c96ab874fe210820025b3857`. It adds one test file and leaves your production implementation unchanged.

It combines the native scheduler / `CPUOffloadingSpec` shared-prefix admission with real CPU↔GPU copies. Two 48-token requests share a 32-token prefix and have different 16-token tails. Synthetic FP16 data is first stored through the native worker, GPU storage is poisoned, and both requests are admitted before worker dispatch.

**Results on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop / SM120, WSL2, driver 592.01, Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1:**

- Sync and async scheduler variants each passed in two fresh processes; one capability opt-out control also passed: **five successful executions of three distinct variants**.
- Each positive execution shared the same two nonempty GPU prefix blocks with refcount two and one logical load job. Native seed-store and load completions each reported **65,536 bytes**.
- Both real request block tables matched independent expected bytes exactly. The test checks guards, CPU source contents, private-tail separation, reference/job cleanup, and successful closure of the saved native mmap handle.
- The opt-out control did not attach in flight; subsequent ordinary cache reuse was allowed. Logical jobs are not physical DMA/kernel counts.

The attachment contains an applicable `TEST_ADDITION.patch`, exact test source, reproduction notes, commands, and the five per-case JSON records and original pytest logs. Two earlier fixture revisions failed before this final version (a pathname-lifetime assumption, then incomplete mmap closure); those runs are not counted as full passes. The successful fixture correction does not establish an upstream leak or the old process’s unique root cause.

**Scope:** model computation is substituted by model-output containers. This does not validate model outputs/accuracy, performance, cancellation/failure, multi-rank, NIXL, current main, or production readiness. Host memory was unpinned on WSL; full-process GPU-memory telemetry was unavailable. Full upstream CI/pre-commit was not run.

**AI disclosure:** Codex prepared the test and executed it on my local GPU. A separate GPT Pro review checked the code and raw evidence offline without repeating GPU execution. This is not an attestation of manual human code review or upstream CI.
